heroHeadline: Trump Rejects Iran Counter-Proposal as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!'; Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire Expires; Warsh Senate Cloture Clears; Beijing Visit May 13
heroSubtitle: On May 11, 2026 (Day 72 of the US-Iran war), President Trump posted on Truth Social calling Iran's formal counter-proposal 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!' and accusing Tehran of 'playing games' — Iran had demanded recognition of Hormuz sovereignty, a separate nuclear track (no dismantlement), sanctions lifted within 30 days, war reparations, and an end to all fronts including Lebanon, while offering only a shortened enrichment halt and partial HEU transfer to a third country; Iran's Foreign Ministry called its terms 'reasonable' and vowed to 'confront its enemies,' the Washington Post described the ceasefire as 'increasingly shaky,' and Brent crude spiked back toward $108–112/bbl, reversing the May 10 peace-optimism easing — Pakistan and Qatar intermediary channels remain active. Separately, the US-brokered 72-hour Russia-Ukraine ceasefire (May 9–11) expired with no extension announced: Russia claimed 16,071 violations by Ukraine, Ukraine documented continued Russian frontline combat including a Kharkiv drone strike injuring 5 civilians (including 2 children aged 8) and 2 killed in Dnipropetrovsk; the 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange was proceeding and US/European officials were 'considering how to steer countries into further talks.' On the domestic front, the Senate cleared cloture on Kevin Warsh's Fed Chair nomination at 5:30 PM ET — with Republicans holding 53 seats and Sen. Fetterman (D-PA) supporting, the final confirmation vote is imminent before Powell's May 15 exit. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs officially confirmed Trump's state visit to Beijing for May 13–15, where the Xi-Trump summit is expected to cover the Iran war, the US-China trade truce extension, rare earths, Taiwan, and Jimmy Lai.
